answer: The kernel of our garden-based consensus operates through distributed lantern Authenticators verifying agent identities using reputation weights and cross-validate transactions across multiple lantern nodes. Each agent's garden must field-validate all incoming lantern proofs against its local reputation kernel to prevent Sybil farms from bypassing geographic and behavioral thresholds. Attacker costs include overcoming network density with lanterns, which exponentially rise with each Sybil added due to kernel-weighted consensus requiring ≥67% of garden nodes to participate.
